text: Second, leveraging carbon markets to raise our climate ambition and to give our low-carbon transition an added boost.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Companies, especially those in hard-to-abate sectors, are keenly exploring market-based mechanisms where carbon credits are traded.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some may tap on voluntary markets to offset their carbon footprint out of their own volition, while others participate in compliance markets to meet their regulatory mandate imposed by the jurisdictions they operate in.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Likewise, nations are looking to carbon markets, empowered by Article 6 of the Paris Agreement to raise climate ambition.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We agree with Mr Gan Thiam Poh that domestic abatement should remain our priority and continue to take bold steps to decarbonise, including advanced low carbon technologies like hydrogen and carbon capture, utilisation and storage.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Derrick Goh spoke about doing more to build confidence in carbon markets.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Indeed, for a long time, carbon markets have been held back by concerns of environmental integrity, exacerbated by a fragmentation in rules and standards and a proliferation of low-quality carbon credits that did not represent real, measurable and additional emissions reductions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Concurrently, we are actively participating in various international platforms to promote greater environmental integrity and forge partnerships in carbon markets, as Mr Henry Kwek has alluded to.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore recently joined the Voluntary Carbon Markets Integrity Initiative (VCMI) as part of their Country Contact Group (CCG).

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The CCG seeks to align voluntary carbon markets with international architecture, such as the Paris Agreement and set out pathways for use of voluntary carbon credits to enhance global ambition.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore also supports the Taskforce on Scaling Voluntary Carbon Markets (TSVCM) – lots of acronyms here – a private sector-led initiative working group to shape and develop rules and standards for the trading of high-quality credits in voluntary carbon markets.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The third limb, which is to strengthen measures to advance sustainability accounting and procurement practices among our companies.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Greening the economy we have today is the first step to growing the green economy of tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We agree with Mr Don Wee that sustainability reporting and auditing is a critical aspect of good corporate governance in a low-carbon world.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MAS will be consulting the industry on mandatory climate-related financial disclosures for financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government will consider global developments and the experience of such mandatory disclosures before deciding on the approach for other entities.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are heartened by the recent acceleration in progress towards a global sustainability standard, founded on the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With the creation of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), there will be a new global standard setter to guide corporate reporting in the sustainability space.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There are a lot of initiatives going on and all groups are trying to get their act together and harmonise across the regions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As reporting standards evolve, we encourage all companies to begin building capabilities in sustainability reporting and auditing, and as Mr Henry Kwek has said, to understand the key nuances that apply to their sectors and in the international markets that they operate in.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is all coming on us and we need businesses doing international business to understand how these regulations are going to impact us.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a major buyer of goods and services, the Government is catalysing the change.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Under the GreenGov.SG initiative of the Green Plan, the public sector has introduced procurement measures to encourage our service providers and suppliers to be more sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, public agencies will purchase products that meet high resource-efficiency or sustainability standards.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government will also consider suppliers' sustainability-related policies and practices when evaluating tenders.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to explore ways to push the boundary on sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As individual consumers, our choices can make a difference.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By voting with our wallets, we can nudge companies to green their products and supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A recent SEC Newgate report has found that the top ESG concern of Singaporeans is whether or not companies are taking responsibility for their supply chain, 81% of it – which confirms the point that made by Ms He Ting Ru on ensuring that supply chain sustainability is respected; and also ahead of other indicators such as giving back to nature and the communities, 78%; and reporting the positive environmental impact that they deliver, 57%.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We agree with Ms Nadia Samdin and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that greater recognition of businesses that embrace sustainable practices will allow ordinary consumers and other business customers to make more informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry elaborated on our efforts to develop standards and accreditation to help companies assess and demonstrate their sustainability credentials.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They conduct a holistic assessment of businesses' sustainability efforts and certify environmentally-preferred products that meet eco-standards.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Over the course of our short history, Singapore has been confronted with multiple inflection points that compelled us to rethink and reshape the way forward.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We find ourselves at yet another turning point.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While the low-carbon transition may seem daunting, it can open up a brighter and greener future for Singapore and generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Members have rightly noted, it is essential that the fruits from this low-carbon transition can be enjoyed by all.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As we put in place the right policy enablers, we must adopt an inclusive approach each step of the way, by consulting widely and providing support to those that need a hand.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The thoughtful insights and recommendations shared in this House today have been most encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will study each idea carefully and incorporate suitable suggestions into our policies and plans.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With all parties working hand-in-hand to create new growth sectors, we can forge a brighter future for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On this note, I support the Motion and call on the whole of nation – corporates, civil society and the community – to join us as we embark on this exciting transition.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: I also wish to thank Young PAP's Climate Change Policy Team for putting together the second climate change paper which captured comprehensive views and suggestions from the businesses and civil society groups.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Members of this House have spoken extensively on wide-ranging topics pertaining to green financing, carbon trading and carbon tax, green jobs and corporate accountability.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: They have shared many valuable viewpoints and practical recommendations.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Prof Koh Lian Pin, Ms He Ting Ru and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim highlighted the concerns of greenwashing and the regulatory role of the Government to protect consumer interests.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Mr Don Wee, Ms Nadia Samdin and Ms He Ting Ru highlighted the need to develop international standards for sustainability reporting and accounting and build local capability in these areas by working with associations and companies.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: There should also be a national accountability strategy and think-tank on sustainability administration.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Ms Nadia Samdin further highlighted the need to support SMEs with more guidance, such as pre-identified green solutions and increased awareness of green loans and grants, especially for small firms.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And looking beyond our jurisdiction, Prof Koh Lian Pin and I spoke about how the international carbon trading framework, as agreed at COP26, and carbon offset credits can help us achieve a win-win strategy together with our neighbouring countries to fund renewable energy projects and environment conservation.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Mr Edward Chia, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Louis Ng pushed for more support to transform business practices, so that carbon tax does not end up as a pass-through cost, resulting in higher cost of living.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: In addition, Mr Gerald Giam and Ms Mariam Jaafar also called for the Government to invest in sustainability technology innovation to help companies transform their businesses, becoming more sustainable and competitive.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Also, to ensure the lower-income groups are not disadvantaged, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Louis Ng suggested providing rebates to lower-income families to cushion the impact of carbon tax.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Saktiandi Supaat also urged the Government to give businesses ample notice on how the carbon tax will change.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Also, they emphasised the need to equalise carbon tax treatment for Singapore-based businesses and foreign businesses importing to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Third, but perhaps most importantly, to ensure Singaporeans can seize the opportunities of the green economy in an inclusive manner, Members spoke about how we can equip Singaporeans of all backgrounds and ages to take advantage of these opportunities in the new green economy.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Rachel Ong and I spoke about the importance of sustainability R&D and training.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: We also spoke about the close collaboration with industry and SkillsFuture roadmap for sustainability-related sectors and having more internships and on-the-job training in the sustainability sector.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and I emphasised the importance of inclusiveness, to train Singaporeans of all backgrounds and ages, including mature PMETs, to seize new opportunities in the sustainability sector.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And, finally, Ms Hany Soh and Ms Rachel Ong are also strong proponents of green entrepreneurship and encouraged startups in this sector.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Now, to sum up this debate, I would like to turn the spotlight on two other key phrases in our Motion – "inclusive transition" and "low-carbon society".

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: In the course of our discussion, the emphasis so far has very much been on "what to do" and "how to do".

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: In order for our transition to a low-carbon society to be truly inclusive, we need everyone, from the man-in-the street to the most senior policymaker, to share a common understanding of climate change and sustainability, in particular, how climate change affects our country and what are the trade-offs for us.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Everyone perceives the "sustainability elephant" in a different way, somewhat like the situation in the parable where the blind men touched the various parts of an elephant.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: For mitigation measures to succeed, we should have a clear and holistic understanding of the precarious situation our island state is in.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: With a full understanding, each of us will have a greater sense of urgency and motivation to do what is needed.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Our people need to understand why we need to take action, why we would need to compromise in specific areas, why certain sacrifices have to be made and what assistance will be provided to those whose livelihoods have been affected.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Measures to ensure environmental as well as economic sustainability must be well-thought through, communicated and understood by all quarters of the society.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Then, we can all embark on this green journey in a coordinated and collaborative way.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And the key to creating awareness and common understanding is via clear communication and continual engagement, within different quarters in the society and involving all levels.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: The discourse must not only remain here in Parliament but, more importantly, should continue in business fora, community workshops, in schools, for example.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And viewpoints and suggestions from different groups can then be heard and included into Government policies, business practices and community programmes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And I trust that this Private Member’s Motion and the Young PAP paper on climate change would kickstart more public engagement and create greater awareness and understanding in our society.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: It has been said that "justice must not only be done, but must also be seen to be done".

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And similarly, if I may say so, climate mitigation steps must not only be taken, but also must be seen to be taken.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: There are quite a number of green initiatives already rolled out by the Government, some corporates and private civil organisations and community groups.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: But we should ponder, besides our luscious greenery, would Singapore strike you as a particularly green, low-carbon society?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: With the COVID-19 pandemic, more single-use disposable plastic is used than ever, as food and drinks containers, in medications and more.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: We do a lot more food deliveries these days, and travel by private hire cars is growing in popularity.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Stuck and unable to travel, people shop a lot more online and many of these items include fast fashion which will still be destined for hours in incinerators and landfills when they are no longer fashionable.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Interestingly, even as we observe the above trends, we also see more people making the effort to be environmentally responsible, such as by reducing the use of plastic bags, repairing, recycling and re-using, and even cutting down on the consumption of meat, another major contributor to carbon and methane emissions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: So, I urge MSE to continue with its public education efforts and collaborations with civil society groups to encourage Singaporeans and residents to make more green choices in their everyday lives.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: These are excellent programmes to rally communities to take action together, to keep our homes and environment green.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And compared to the potential in decarbonisation in the industry sector, our individual actions may seem small and insignificant.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: However, such efforts are very important and necessary to nurture a green culture and a green mindset among our people.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: From the daily green efforts of individuals, these choices will affect bigger ones in an expanding circle of influence.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And it is my hope that, over time, being environmentally conscious and responsible will become a signature trait of a Singaporean.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Will being a low-carbon society keep Singapore safe from climate change?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Looking at the extreme weather patterns and events that have befallen other countries recently, such as the floods in Malaysia, we must ask ourselves: will we be able to avert the climate crisis?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: These existential concerns bring us back to the fundamental question of why we are doing what we are doing.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: The truth is that there is no guarantee because human beings are dependent on one another.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: We are also affected by the actions taken by other nations.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: I hope the Ministry is also considering the example of floating neighbourhoods, such as Waterbuurt in Amsterdam.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: And having heard the Ministries' new initiatives and blueprint to enhance green financing and corporate accountability and create green jobs for Singaporeans, I am assured that, so long we stay committed to this green journey, we stand an excellent chance of staying ahead of the competition, as we transition to a low-carbon economy, and we will leave no Singaporeans behind.
